docs.title: At a glance
docs.snippet: Designed with simplicity and type-safety in mind, Elysia offers a familiar API with extensive support for TypeScript and is optimized for Bun.

docs.title: Performance
docs.snippet: Building on Bun and extensive optimization like static code analysis allows Elysia to generate optimized code on the fly.

docs.title: TypeScript
docs.snippet: Elysia's Type System is fine-tuned to infer types from your code automatically, without needing to write explicit TypeScript, while providing type-safety at both runtime and compile time for the most ergonomic developer experience.

docs.title: Type Integrity
docs.snippet: To take it a step further, Elysia provides **Elysia.t**, a schema builder to validate types and values at both runtime and compile time, creating a single source of truth for your data types.

docs.title: Standard Schema
docs.snippet: Elysia supports Standard Schema, allowing you to use your favorite validation library:

docs.title: OpenAPI
docs.snippet: Elysia adopts many standards by default, like OpenAPI, WinterTC compliance, and Standard Schema. Allowing you to integrate with most of the industry standard tools or at least easily integrate with tools you are familiar with.

docs.title: OpenAPI from types
docs.heading_path: At a glance > OpenAPI from types
docs.snippet: Elysia also supports OpenAPI schema generation with **1 line directly from types**.

docs.title: End-to-end Type Safety
docs.heading_path: At a glance > End-to-end Type Safety
docs.snippet: With Elysia, you can synchronize your types with your frontend team automatically, similar to tRPC, using Elysia's client library, "Eden".

docs.title: Type Soundness
docs.snippet: Most frameworks with end-to-end type safety usually assume only a happy part, leaving error handling and edge cases out of the type system.

docs.title: Platform Agnostic
docs.snippet: * Bun * Node.js * Deno * Cloudflare Worker * Vercel * Expo via API routes * Nextjs via API routes * Astro via API routes

docs.title: Our Community
docs.snippet: We want to create a friendly and welcoming community for everyone with bright, cute, friendly and playful design including our hand drawn anime girl mascot, *"Elysia chan"*.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.snippet: Elysia is a TypeScript backend framework with multiple runtime support but optimized for Bun.

docs.title: Routing
docs.snippet: Web servers use the request's **path and method** to look up the correct resource, known as **"routing"**.

docs.title: Path type
docs.snippet: * **static paths** - static strings to locate the resource * **dynamic paths** - segments can be any value * **wildcards** - path until a specific point can be anything

docs.title: Static Path
docs.snippet: Static Path

docs.title: Dynamic path
docs.snippet: Dynamic paths match some part and capture the value to extract extra information.

docs.title: Multiple path parameters
docs.heading_path: Routing  > Dynamic path > Multiple path parameters
docs.snippet: You can have as many path parameters as you like, which will then be stored into a params object.

docs.title: Optional path parameters
docs.snippet: We can make a path parameter optional by adding a question mark ? after the parameter name.

docs.title: Wildcards
docs.snippet: Dynamic paths allow capturing a single segment while wildcards allow capturing the rest of the path.

docs.title: Path priority
docs.snippet: If both a static and a dynamic path are present, Elysia will resolve the static path rather than the dynamic path.

docs.title: HTTP Verb
docs.snippet: HTTP defines a set of request methods to indicate the desired action to be performed for a given resource

docs.title: DELETE
docs.snippet: To handle each of the different verbs, Elysia has a built-in API for several HTTP verbs by default, similar to Elysia.get

docs.title: Custom Method
docs.snippet: const app = new Elysia()  .get('/get', 'hello')  .post('/post', 'hi')  .route('M-SEARCH', '/m-search', 'connect') // [!code ++]  .listen(3000)

docs.title: ALL method
docs.snippet: Elysia provides an Elysia.all for handling any HTTP method for a specified path using the same API like **Elysia.get** and **Elysia.post**

docs.title: Prefix
docs.snippet: We can separate a group into a separate plugin instance to reduce nesting by providing a **prefix** to the constructor.

docs.title: Handler
docs.snippet: new Elysia()  // the function () => 'hello world' is a handler  .get('/', () => 'hello world')  .listen(3000)

docs.title: Context
docs.snippet: **Context** contains request information which is unique for each request, and is not shared except for store (global mutable state).

docs.title: Property
docs.snippet: * **body** - HTTP message, form or file upload. * **query** - Query String, includes additional parameters for search query as JavaScript Object. (Query is extracted from a value after pathname starting from '?' question mark sign) * **params** - Elysia's path parameters parsed…

docs.title: Utility Function
docs.snippet: * **redirect** - A function to redirect a response * **status** - A function to return custom status code * **set** - Property to apply to Response:  * **headers** - Response headers

docs.title: Additional Property
docs.snippet: * **request** - Web Standard Request * **server** - Bun server instance * **path** - Pathname of the request

docs.title: status
docs.snippet: new Elysia()  .get('/', ({ status }) => status(418, "Kirifuji Nagisa"))  .listen(3000)

docs.title: Set
docs.snippet: new Elysia()  .get('/', ({ set, status }) => {  set.headers = { 'X-Teapot': 'true' }

docs.title: set.headers
docs.snippet: ::: tip Elysia provides auto-completion for lowercase for case-sensitivity consistency, eg. use set-cookie rather than Set-Cookie. :::

docs.title: Cookie
docs.snippet: There's no need for get/set; you can extract the cookie name and retrieve or update its value directly.

docs.title: Redirect
docs.snippet: new Elysia()  .get('/', ({ redirect }) => {  return redirect('https://youtu.be/whpVWVWBW4U?&t=8')  })  .get('/custom-status', ({ redirect }) => {  // You can also set custom status to redirect  return redirect('https://youtu.be/whpVWVWBW4U?&t=8', 302)  })  .listen(3000)

docs.title: Formdata
docs.snippet: We can return a FormData by returning the form utility directly from the handler.

docs.title: Return a file
docs.snippet: Or alternatively, you can return a single file by returning file directly without form.

docs.title: Stream
docs.snippet: To return a response streaming out of the box, use a generator function with the yield keyword.

docs.title: Server Sent Events (SSE)
docs.snippet: new Elysia()  .get('/sse', function* () {  yield sse('hello world')  yield sse({  event: 'message',  data: {  message: 'This is a message',  timestamp: new Date().toISOString()  },  })  })

docs.title: Conditional Stream
docs.heading_path: Handler  > Server Sent Events (SSE) > Conditional Stream
docs.snippet: If the response is returned without yield, Elysia will automatically convert stream to normal response instead.

docs.title: Automatic cancellation
docs.heading_path: Handler  > Server Sent Events (SSE) > Automatic cancellation
docs.snippet: Before response streaming is completed, if the user cancels the request, Elysia will automatically stop the generator function.

docs.title: Eden
docs.snippet: Eden will interpret a stream response as AsyncGenerator allowing us to use for await loop to consume the stream.

docs.title: Request
docs.snippet: Elysia is built on top of Web Standard Request which is shared between multiple runtime like Node, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Worker, Vercel Edge Function, and more.

docs.title: Server Bun only
docs.snippet: Server instance is a Bun server instance, allowing us to access server information like port number or request IP.

docs.title: Request IP Bun only
docs.heading_path: Handler  > Server Bun only > Request IP Bun only
docs.snippet: new Elysia()  .get('/ip', ({ server, request }) => {  return server?.requestIP(request)  })  .listen(3000)

docs.title: Extending context Advanced concept
docs.snippet: Elysia provides a minimal Context by default, allowing you to extend the Context for your specific needs using state, decorate, derive, and resolve.

docs.title: Plugin
docs.snippet: Every Elysia instance can run independently or be used as part of another instance.

docs.title: Dependency
docs.snippet: Elysia, by design, is composed of multiple mini Elysia apps which can run **independently** like microservices that communicate with each other.

docs.title: Deduplication
docs.snippet: By default, each plugin will be re-executed **every time** applying to another instance.

docs.title: Global vs Explicit Dependency
docs.heading_path: Plugin  > Dependency  > Global vs Explicit Dependency

docs.title: Scope
docs.snippet: This means if you create a new instance, it will not share the lifecycle methods with other instances.

docs.title: Scope level
docs.snippet: 1. **local** (default) - applies to the current instance and its descendants only 2. **scoped** - applies to the parent, current instance, and descendants 3. **global** - applies to all instances that use the plugin (all parents, current, and descendants)

docs.title: Descendant
docs.snippet: If the hook is registered in a plugin, instances that use the plugin will **NOT** inherit hooks and schema.

docs.title: Config
docs.snippet: To make the plugin more useful, allowing customization via config is recommended.

docs.title: Functional callback
docs.snippet: It's recommended to define a new plugin instance instead of using a function callback.

docs.snippet: typescript twoslash const signUp = <T>(a: T) => a const signIn = <T>(a: T) => a const isUserExists = <T>(a: T) => a // ---cut--- import { Elysia, t } from 'elysia'

docs.title: Grouped Guard
docs.snippet: With the same API as guard apply to the 2nd parameter, instead of nesting group and guard together.

docs.title: Scope cast Advanced Concept
docs.snippet: 1. inline as applies to only a single hook 2. guard as applies to all hooks in a guard 3. instance as applies to all hooks in an instance

docs.title: Inline as
docs.heading_path: Plugin  > Scope cast Advanced Concept > Inline as

docs.title: Guard as
docs.heading_path: Plugin  > Scope cast Advanced Concept > Guard as
docs.snippet: const plugin = new Elysia()  .guard({  as: 'scoped', // [!code ++]  response: t.String(),  beforeHandle() {  console.log('ok')  }  })  .get('/child', 'ok')

docs.title: Instance as
docs.heading_path: Plugin  > Scope cast Advanced Concept > Instance as
docs.snippet: const plugin = new Elysia()  .derive(() => {  return { hi: 'ok' }  })  .get('/child', ({ hi }) => hi)  .as('scoped') // [!code ++]

docs.title: Deferred Module
docs.snippet: The deferred module is an async plugin that can be registered after the server is started.

docs.title: Testing

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.snippet: Instead of a sequential process, Elysia's request handling is divided into multiple stages called **lifecycle events**.

docs.title: Why
docs.snippet: Normally, we’d set the **"Content-Type"** header to **"text/html"** so the browser can render it.

docs.title: Hook
docs.snippet: 1. Local Hook: Execute on a specific route 2. Interceptor Hook: Execute on every route **after the hook is registered**

docs.title: Local Hook
docs.snippet:
new Elysia() .get('/', () => '

Hello World

', { afterHandle({ responseValue, set }) { if (isHtml(responseValue)) set.headers['Content-Type'] = 'text/html; charset=utf8' } }) .get('/hi', () => '

Hello World

') .listen(3000)

docs.title: Interceptor Hook
docs.snippet: To add an interceptor hook, you can use .on followed by a lifecycle event in camelCase:

docs.title: Order of code
docs.snippet: new Elysia()  .onBeforeHandle(() => {  console.log('1')  })  .get('/', () => 'hi')  .onBeforeHandle(() => {  console.log('2')  })  .listen(3000)

docs.title: Request
docs.snippet: As onRequest is designed to provide only the most crucial context to reduce overhead, it is recommended to use in the following scenarios:

docs.title: Example
docs.snippet: new Elysia()  .use(rateLimiter)  .onRequest(({ rateLimiter, ip, set, status }) => {  if (rateLimiter.check(ip)) return status(420, 'Enhance your calm')  })  .get('/', () => 'hi')  .listen(3000)

docs.title: Pre Context
docs.snippet: The onRequest context is typed as PreContext, a minimal representation of Context with the following attributes: request: Request

docs.title: Parse
docs.snippet: A function to parse the body; the return value will be appended to Context.body. If not, Elysia will continue iterating through additional parser functions assigned by onParse until either body is assigned or all parsers have been executed.

docs.title: Example
docs.snippet: new Elysia().onParse(({ request, contentType }) => {  if (contentType === 'application/custom-type') return request.text() })

docs.title: Context
docs.snippet: All of the context is based on normal context and can be used like normal context in route handler.

docs.title: Parser
docs.snippet: By default, Elysia will try to determine body parsing function ahead of time and pick the most suitable function to speed up the process.

docs.title: Explicit Parser
docs.snippet: However, in some scenarios if Elysia fails to pick the correct body parser function, we can explicitly tell Elysia to use a certain function by specifying type.

docs.title: Skip Body Parsing
docs.snippet: When you need to integrate a third-party library with an HTTP handler like trpc or orpc, and it throws Body is already used.

docs.title: Custom Parser
docs.snippet: new Elysia()  .parser('custom', ({ request, contentType }) => {  if (contentType === 'application/elysia') return request.text()  })  .post('/', ({ body }) => body, {  parse: ['custom', 'json']  })

docs.title: Transform
docs.snippet: Executed just before **Validation** process, designed to mutate context to conform with the validation or appending new value.

docs.title: Example
docs.snippet: new Elysia()  .get('/id/:id', ({ params: { id } }) => id, {  params: t.Object({  id: t.Number()  }),  transform({ params }) {  const id = +params.id

docs.title: Derive
docs.snippet: Append new value to context directly **before validation**. It's stored in the same stack as **transform**.

docs.title: Queue
docs.snippet: new Elysia()  .onTransform(() => {  console.log(1)  })  .derive(() => {  console.log(2)

docs.title: Before Handle
docs.snippet: Designed to provide a custom validation to provide a specific requirement before running the main handler.

docs.title: Example
docs.snippet: typescript import { Elysia } from 'elysia' import { validateSession } from './user'

docs.title: Guard
docs.snippet: When we need to apply the same before handle to multiple routes, we can use guard to apply the same before handle to multiple routes.

docs.title: Resolve
docs.snippet: Append new value to context **after validation**. It's stored in the same stack as **beforeHandle**.

docs.title: Guard resolve
docs.snippet: As resolve is not available in local hook, it's recommended to use guard to encapsulate the **resolve** event.

docs.title: After Handle
docs.snippet: Execute after the main handler, for mapping a returned value of **before handle** and **route handler** into a proper response.

docs.title: Example
docs.snippet: Below is an example of using the after handle to add HTML content type to response headers.

docs.title: Returned Value
docs.snippet: If a value is returned After Handle will use a return value as a new response value unless the value is **undefined**

docs.title: Context
docs.snippet: onAfterHandle context extends from Context with the additional property of response, which is the response to return to the client.

docs.title: Map Response
docs.snippet: Executed just after **"afterHandle"**, designed to provide custom response mapping.

docs.title: Example
docs.snippet: new Elysia()  .mapResponse(({ responseValue, set }) => {  const isJson = typeof responseValue === 'object'

docs.title: On Error (Error Handling)
docs.snippet: Designed for error handling. It will be executed when an error is thrown in any lifecycle.

docs.title: Example
docs.snippet: Elysia catches all the errors thrown in the handler, classifies the error code, and pipes them to onError middleware.

docs.title: Custom 404 message
docs.heading_path: Lifecycle  > On Error (Error Handling) > Custom 404 message
docs.snippet: new Elysia()  .onError(({ code, status, set }) => {  if (code === 'NOT_FOUND') return status(404, 'Not Found :(')  })  .post('/', () => {  throw new NotFoundError()  })  .listen(3000)

docs.title: Context
docs.snippet: Context

docs.title: Error Code
docs.heading_path: Lifecycle  > On Error (Error Handling) > Error Code
docs.snippet: * **NOT\_FOUND** * **PARSE** * **VALIDATION** * **INTERNAL\_SERVER\_ERROR** * **INVALID\_COOKIE\_SIGNATURE** * **INVALID\_FILE\_TYPE** * **UNKNOWN** * **number** (based on HTTP Status)

docs.title: Local Error
docs.heading_path: Lifecycle  > On Error (Error Handling) > Local Error
docs.snippet: new Elysia()  .get('/', () => 'Hello', {  beforeHandle({ set, request: { headers }, error }) {  if (!isSignIn(headers)) throw error(401)  },  error() {  return 'Handled'  }  })  .listen(3000)

docs.snippet: After Response

docs.title: Example
docs.snippet: new Elysia()  .onAfterResponse(() => {  console.log('Response', performance.now())  })  .listen(3000)

docs.title: Response
docs.snippet: new Elysia()  .onAfterResponse(({ responseValue }) => {  console.log(responseValue)  })  .get('/', () => 'Hello')  .listen(3000)
